K-Fold Cross-Validation for GMM Model Selection

Source: R/cross-validation.R
gmm_cv.Rd

Performs k-fold cross-validation to evaluate and compare growth mixture models with different numbers of classes. Properly accounts for complex survey design by maintaining design integrity within folds.

Usage

gmm_cv(
  data,
  id,
  time,
  outcome,
  classes = 1:5,
  k_folds = 10,
  growth_model = "linear",
  strata = NULL,
  cluster = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  stratified_cv = TRUE,
  starts = 200,
  cores = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

Data frame in long format

id

Character string naming ID variable

time

Character string naming time variable

outcome

Character string naming outcome variable

classes

Integer vector specifying number of classes to test (e.g., 1:5)

k_folds

Integer number of folds (default = 10)

growth_model

Character string: "linear" or "quadratic"

strata

Optional character string naming stratification variable

cluster

Optional character string naming cluster variable

weights

Optional character string naming weight variable

covariates

Optional character vector naming covariates

stratified_cv

Logical; if TRUE, maintains stratum proportions in folds

starts

Integer number of random starts per model

cores

Integer number of CPU cores for parallel processing

seed

Integer random seed for reproducibility

verbose

Logical; print progress?

Value

An S4 object of class GMM_CrossValidation with slots:

cv_results

Data frame with metrics for each fold and class count

summary_stats

Aggregated statistics across folds

best_k

Recommended number of classes

fold_assignments

Vector indicating fold membership for each individual

detailed_results

List with full results for each fold

Details

Cross-validation for mixture models requires special considerations:

**1. Survey Design Preservation:** When stratified_cv = TRUE, folds maintain the proportion of observations from each stratum, preserving the survey design structure.

**2. Individual-Level Splitting:** The data is split at the individual level (not observation level) to keep all time points for each person together.

**3. Prediction Metrics:** Multiple metrics are computed: - Log-likelihood on held-out data - Classification accuracy (if true classes known) - Mean squared prediction error - Weighted metrics using survey weights

**4. Label Switching:** Class labels may differ across folds. The algorithm attempts to align labels based on trajectory patterns.

References

Merkle, E. C., You, D., & Preacher, K. (2016). Testing non-nested structural equation models. *Psychological Methods*, 21(2), 151-163.

Nylund-Gibson, K., & Choi, A. Y. (2018). Ten frequently asked questions about latent class analysis. *Translational Issues in Psychological Science*, 4(4), 440-461.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data(mcs_simulated)

# 3-fold CV comparing 1-2 class models (lighter for examples)
cv_results <- gmm_cv(
  data = mcs_simulated,
  id = "id",
  time = "age",
  outcome = "selfcontrol",
  classes = 1:2,
  k_folds = 3,
  strata = "stratum",
  cluster = "cluster",
  weights = "weight",
  stratified_cv = TRUE,
  starts = 20,  # Reduced for faster execution
  cores = 1,    # Sequential for stability in examples
  seed = 123
)

print(cv_results)
plot(cv_results)
} # }
